MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 12, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:30 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant t0 AB 361 and teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 5:30 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:31 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated li_tigation

  Code Section 54956.9

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated litigation

  2.  Significant exposure to litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
  54956.9(d)(2)
  Development Agreement between the City of Malibu and La Paz Ranch, LLC,
  regarding the property located at 23465 Civic Center Way
  Number of Cases: (1)

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 6:43 p.m.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 12, 2023
  Page 2 of 13

W x  ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attorney; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Kristin Riesgo,
  Community Services Director; Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Susan Duenas, Public
  Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Matt Myerhoff, Media Information
  Officer; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City Clerk; Christina Munoz, Deputy City Clerk; Kate
  Manisco, Recreation Manager; Luis Flores, Public Safety Liaison; Sarah Flores,
  Emergency Services Coordinator; and Brandie Ayala, Administrative Analyst

  CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attorney Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:30 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Sections
  54956.9(d)(2) and 54956.9(d)(4), with all Councilmembers present. He stated the Council
  discussed the items on the Closed Session agenda and took no reportable action.

  REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on June
  2, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on June 9, 2023.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  City Clerk Pettijohn led the Pledge of Allegiance.

  APPROVAL OF AGENDA

  MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda, continuing Item No. l.A. to a date uncertain, hearing Item
  No. 7.A. after the Consent Calendar, hearing Item No. 6.A. after 7.A., and
  adjourning in memory of Leah Isaacs and Barry Hilton. The question was called,
  and the motion carried unanimously.

  ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A.  Presentation of 2023 Jake Kuredjian Citizenship Award

  This item was continued to a date uncertain upon approval of the agenda.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 12, 2023
  Page 3 of 13

M  ‘  Recognition of Public Safety Responders

  Mayor Silverstein recognized the City’s Public Safety Responders with thank you
  books.

  Public Safety Director Duefias thanked the City’s Public Safety Responders and
  staff for their efforts at the recent public safety expo.

  ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Ryan Embree discussed the antenna pole at Santa Monica College and permitting
  conditions and stated that its location conflicted with use of the nearby helicopter
  pad. He requested an explanation from Los Angeles County of the necessity ofthe
  pole since transmission with the shorter interim pole was possible for three years.
  He stated that the County’s application to the City stated that the pole would be
  used for emergencies which conflicted with regular expanded semi-commercial use
  that was not disclosed adequately at the concept was approved.

  Jo Drummond thanked the Council for adjourning in memory of Leah Isaacs. She
  discussed the radio tower at Santa Monica College and requested the

U
  Telecommunication Commission be reinstated or the Public Works Commission
  begin reviewing telecommunications projects.

  ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Kylie and Logan Epstein, Youth Commission, provided an update on Fiscal Year
  2022-23 accomplishments, which included a food drive for the Boys and Girls Club
  Thanksgiving baskets, voter registration public service announcements, a Cinema
  Malibu movie night sock collection drive for Socks of Love, toy collection for the
  Los Angeles County Fire Department Foundation, hosting a youth government
  summit, a baby diaper and wipes drive for Safe Place for Youth Venice, toiletry
  items collection for the People’s Concem, and participation in a virtual organics
  recycling workshop. They stated that they volunteered at special events which
  included Tiny Tot Olympics, Breakfast with Santa, and Chumash Day. They stated
  that they collected more than 400 items that benefited local nonprofit organizations,
  provided more than 200 hours of community service, and thanked the Council for
  providing the opportunity to represent the youth of Malibu.

  Public Safety Manager Duefias discussed the June 12, 2023 Public Safety Expo and
  Public Safety Responder Appreciation Day. She stated that it was well attended and
  featured organizations including the Community Emergency Response Team
  (CERT), Arson Watch, Volunteers on Patrol (VOP), Los Angeles County Fire
  Department, Department of Forestry, and Cal Tech. She stated that there were
  demonstrations and presentations, which included fire extinguisher education, an
  earthquake simulator, a free tree giveaway, emergency generator raffle, and food
  vendors. She stated that most costs were paid for by a fire prevention grant from
  Cal Fire and recognized staff efforts and Councilmember participation in the event.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 12, 2023
  Page 4 of 13

City Manager McClary thanked City staff for their efforts and stated that the event
was well received by the community.

Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, thanked the
Council for honoring emergency responders. He provided an update on the May
2023 statistics and reported part one crimes were reduced by 18 percent from the
same time the prior year and stated there was a downward trend of burglaries. He
reported there were two incidents where multiple vehicles were broken into and
two vehicles stolen, one of which was recovered. He stated that a suspect vehicle
was identified in the second incident and suspects were outstanding. He stated that
they conducted a parking enforcement operation overnight the prior Thursday,
which resulted in 91 citations issued and six vehicles towed. He stated that they
worked with VOPs, special assignment deputies, and Public Safety Liaison Flores.
He discussed an experience with an individual experiencing homelessness who was
connected to services through Public Safety Liaison Flores. He stated that the beach
team had begun to patrol on weekends and would be full-time beginning in July.
He provided statistics year to date and reported 188 citations were issued for
possession of alcohol on the beach, 45 citations for dogs on the beach, 204 traffic
citations, 1,382 parking citations, and 186 vehicles towed. He discussed racing on
Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) and reported that during the Aids/LifeCycle event
held the previous Saturday with approximately 2,000 bicycle riders on PCH,
deputies observed two Lamborghini vehicles traveling at a high rate of speed near
Las Flores, without registration and one without insurance and both drivers were
cited, and vehicles impounded. He stated that a saturation patrol and racing
enforcement operation was planned for an upcoming night when much ofthe racing
occurred.

Mayor Silverstein thanked the Sheriff Department for their work and stated that
Malibu was a relatively safe place to begin with and credited the SheriffDepartment
presence for continuing to keep the community safe.

In response to Mayor Silverstein, Sergeant Soderlund stated that there was a
combination of factors that went into towing a vehicle versus a citation being
issued, which included reckless driving, speed limit, presence of pedestrians or
schools in the area, and traffic volume. He stated that the vehicle could be
impounded if the deputy determined they were driving in a reckless manner.

City Manager McClary stated that he attended the middle school and high school
graduations and attended the Commissioner Brown Act training. He discussed the
Blue Flag environmental award presented to Westward Beach and announced that
the Little League temporary snack shack was operational. He discussed a sewage
spill that occurred the past week on Malibu Canyon Road which was caused by a
car accident. He provided an update on the Trancas Bridge replacement project and
stated that they were pressing Caltrans for safety and pavement improvements, and
it was expected that pothole repair would be conducted in June 2023. He welcomed
and introduced the two new Deputy City Clerks, Christina Munoz, and Jason
Lawrence. He reported that the temporary tow yard at Malibu High School opened
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 12, 2023
  Page 5 of 13

  0n May 27, 2023, and approximately 90 vehicles were towed. He provided an
  update on Woolsey Fire rebuilds with 128 single family homes completed and 258
  a
  with building permits issued. He announced meeting for Malibu Creek ecosystem
  restoration project, hosted by California State Parks and Cal Trout, would be held
  at City Hall on Tuesday, June 13, 2023, from 6:00 p.m. to 8:00 p.m.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti commented on the watershed improvement project that
  involved removal of the Rindge Dam and encouraged public participation in the
  upcoming informational meeting. He discussed the Blue Flag award at Westward
  Beach and encouraged the community to visit and appreciate the scenic location.
  He reported that he attended the middle school and high school graduation
  ceremonies and stated that the students deserved credit for their accomplishments
  and wished them well. He stated that he attended the recent Brown Act training and
  stated that there were changes in the law and he found the information valuable.

  Councilmember Riggins reported that she attended a Clean Power Alliance Board
  meeting, where Malibu was honored as one ofthe first cities that joined. She stated
  that she attended the Little League parade and closing ceremonies on June 3, 2023,
  and thanked league president Nick Shurgot, Jake Lingo, Alicia Peak, Dane
  Skophammer, and City stafffor their efforts. She reported that she attended the high
  school and middle school graduation ceremonies and stated that principals Patrick
  Miller and Melisa Andino did a greatjob with students. She stated she attended the
  Public Safety Expo and“thanked the City’s Public Safety Department staff and
  expressed her appreciation for the City’s safety partners. She stated she attended
  the Brown Act training and found it informative. She stated that she attended the
  Blue Flag presentation at Westward Beach and stated that it was an honor for the
  community to be recognized. She thanked the Youth Commissioners for their
  service and City staff for their support. She stated that she participated in a ride
  along and toured the Lost Hills Sheriff Station. She discussed the Los Angeles
  Metro congestion pricing study, specifically the route on the 10 Freeway from
  downtown Los Angeles to Santa Monica. She stated that anyone who traveled to
  Malibu would be impacted and encouraged the community to provide feedback to
  Metro. She thanked City Manager McClary for providing information on the
  sewage spill.

  Councilmember Stewart discussed the temporary tow yard and thanked everyone
  involved in its success. He discussed the Blue Flag award ceremony held at
  Westward Beach and stated that visiting the location was a moving experience. He
  stated that he attended the workplan meeting held on May 24, 2023. He stated that
  he attended a kindness event and signed the Boys and Girls Club Kindness Mural
  and commended the organization for their positive impact on the community. He
  reported that he attended the Brown Act training and the Public Safety Expo. He
  stated he met with the VOPs and Sheriff Deputies during one oftheir night sweeps
  and commended those who worked the night shift. He discussed the 2023 Poetry
  and Art Student Anthology and encouraged the community to pick one up.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 12, 2023
  Page 6 of 13

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring thanked Sergeant Sutherland for his report and stated that
  the results needed to be publicized to the community. He stated he participated in
  the Califomia Strategies meetings. He stated he attended the Little League parade,
  and everyone enjoyed themselves. He encouraged community involvement in the
  meeting to discuss removal ofthe Rindge Dam. He thanked City Manager McClary
  for providing infonnation on the sewage spill. He discussed an article he recently
  read in the Orange County Register regarding declining school enrollment, and
  referenced the Parks and Recreation master plan report with its proj ection of
  declining birth rates and stated that attention should be paid to the issue.

  Mayor Silverstein discussed the radio tower at Santa Moncia College and stated
  that it was an insult to Malibu and hoped for continued discussions toward a
  solution. He stated that he attended many of the events that others described. He
  stated he attended the Little League event, and that it was enj oyable. He stated that
  declining school enrollment indicated that Malibu was probably overpaying for
  being a part of the Santa Monica-Malibu Unified School District and it was an
  argument for separation.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring stated he met with Sycamore Park residents and saw the
  Mountains Recreation and Conservation Authority (MRCA) signs and trail maps
  to Escondido trail. He questioned the validity of the trail, since in May 2016, the
  City Council voted to abandon trails heading to Ramirez Canyon and Escondido.
  He provided compiled information for the City Attorney’s review regarding the
  status of the trail and the signage placed by the MRCA.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

  Item Nos. 3.B.9. and 3.B.10. were pulled by the Council.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar, pulling Item Nos. 3.B.9. and 3.B.10. The question
  was called, and the motion carried unanimously, Councilmember Stewart
  abstaining from Item No. 3.B.3.

  names, for the purposes stated on the respective demands in a total amount

The following items were pulled from the consent calendar for individual consideration:

  9.  Amendments to the Professional Services Agreements for School District
  Separation
  Recommended Action: 1) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No.
  7 to the Professional Services Agreement with Kirk-Carter and Associates;

  and 2) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 7 to the
  Professional Services Agreement with STLR Corp, dba Ryland School
  Business Consulting.

  The Council discussed the item.

MOTION  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring moved, Councilmember Riggins second a motion
  to: l) Authorize the Mayor to execute Amendment No. 7 to the Professional

  10.  Investment Report for the Month Ending_April 30, 2023
  Recommended Action: Receive the Investment Report for the month ending

  The Council discussed the item.

  The Council received the Investment Report for the month ending April 30,
  2023.

ITEM 7  COUNCIL ITEMS

  2023-2024 Harry Barovsky Memorial Youth Commission Appointments
  Recommended Action: Appoint Commissioners to the 2023-2024 Harry Barovsky
  Memorial Youth Commission.

  Recreation Manager Gallo presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Preston Lilly

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Stewart seconded a motion
  to appoint the following 17 Commissioners to the 2023-2024 Harry Barovsky
  Memorial Youth Commission: Anniston Aragon, Allegra Barzan, Tyler Button,
  Kylie Epstein, Logan Epstein, Hiram Florendo, Maya Guzman, Tanner Kies, Travis
  Kies, Kailyn Lilly, Preston Lilly, Chloe Loquet, Michael Maischoss, Hank Norby,
  Axel Polito, Layla Polito, and Payton Pollack. The question was called, and the
  motion carried unanimously.

ITEM 6  NEW BUSINESS
   Malibu City Council

  A.  Malibu Library Set Aside Fund for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 (Continued from MaV
  22, 2023)
  Recommended Action: Approve the use of Set Aside Funds for the Malibu Library
  for Fiscal Year 2023-2024.

  Assistant City Manager Toney presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speaker: Jo Drummond

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion

ITEM 4  ORDINANCES AND PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A.  Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Wastewater Service Charges
  Recommended Action: 1) Conduct the Public Hearing to receive public testimony
  and consider all protest concerning the adoption of the Engineer’s Report regarding
  the levy of wastewater services fees through property taxes; and 2) Unless there are
  protests from majority of the affected property owners, adopt Resolution No. 23-
  28 approving the Engineer’s Report and collection of wastewater services charges
  on the county tax roll for FiscalYear 2023-2024 for City of Malibu Assessment
  District No. 20 l 5-1 (Civic Center Wastewater Treatment Facility — Phase-1).

  Public Works Director DuBoux and Administrative Analyst Ayala presented the
  staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moVed, and Mayor Pro Tem Uhring seconded a motion to
  adopt Resolution No. 23-28 approving the Engineer’s Report and collection of
  wastewater services charges on the county tax roll for Fiscal Year 2023-2024 for
  City of Malibu Assessment District No. 2015-1 (Civic Center Wastewater
  Treatment Facility — Phase-l). The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

ITEM 5  OLD BUSINESS
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 12, 2023
  Page 10 of 13

  A.  Review of the Hybrid Meeting Pilot Program and Commission Meeting Transition
  Plan
  Recommended Action: 1) Consider the success of the hybrid meeting pilot
  program; 2) Provide direction on the format of City Council meetings, if
  appropriate; and 3) Provide direction on the meeting format for Commission,
  Committee, and Board meetings.

  City Clerk Pettij ohn presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Ryan Embree and Jo Drummond

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved to direct staff to begin scheduling Planning
  Commission meetings as hybrid meetings pursuant to AB 361, recommend
  Planning Commissioners resume meeting in-person; and determine the Council
  would revisit the meeting format for the other Commissions and Committees.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Stewart seconded the motion and moved to direct staff to begin
  scheduling Planning Commission meetings as hybrid meetings beginning with the
  July 17, 2023 Regular Planning Commission meeting.

  The amendment was accepted by the maker of the motion.

  The Council discussed the amended motion and directed questions to staff.

  The question was called, and the amended motion carried unanimously.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Riggins seconded a motion to direct
  that hybrid meeting procedures allow members of the public participating in the
  meeting in-person to surrender their opportunity to speak on an item by deferring
  one minute to another speaker, not to exceed an additional five minutes for any
  individual speaker. The question was called, and the motion carried unanimously.

RECESS  At 8:31 p.m., Mayor Silverstein recessed the meeting. The meeting resumed at 8:42
  p.m. with all Councilmembers present.
  B.  Update Regarding Local Coastal Program Amendment No. 16-006 (Sea View
  Hotel Proiect)
  Recommended Action:  Provide direction to staff on processing fee
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 12, 2023
  Page 11 of 13

  waiver/reduction requests for public access or habitat restoration projects requiring
  a Coastal Development Permit (CDP). Pursuant to 2022 legislation — Assembly Bill
  (AB) 2160 — an applicant who is a public agency or nonprofit organization may
  request that the City waive or reduce a coastal development permit fee for a public
  access project or habitat restoration project. If the request is denied, the applicant
  may bypass City processing and submit the CDP application directly to the
  California Coastal Commission.

  Planning Director Mollica presented the staff report.

  The Council directed questions to staff.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Norm Haynie, Robert Gold, Jefferson Wagner, John Payne, and Jo
  Drummond

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein retumed the matter to
  the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to direct staff to bring back at the June 26, 2023 Regular City Council meeting an
  ordinance to accept the modified Local Coastal Program Amendment No. 16-006.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff, Mr. Gold, and Mr.
  Wagner.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Mayor Silverstein moved to bring back the ordinance only if the CCC agrees to
  direct the money to the City of Malibu or allows the City veto power over how the
  money is used.

  The amendment was not accepted by the maker of the seconder of the motion.

  The Council discussed the motion.

  The question was called, and the motion carried 4-1, Mayor Silverstein opposed.

  NEW BUSINESS (Continued)

  Processing Fee Requests per Assembly Bill 2160
  Recommended Action:  Provide direction to staff on processing fee
  waiver/reduction requests for public access or habitat restoration projects requiring
  a Coastal Development Permit (CDP). Pursuant to 2022 legislation — Assembly Bill
  (AB) 2160 — an applicant who is a public agency or nonprofit organization may
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 12, 2023
  Page 12 of 13

  request that the City waive or reduce a coastal development permit fee for a public
  access project or habitat restoration project. If the request is denied, the applicant
  may bypass City processing and submit the CDP application directly to the
  California Coastal Commission.

  Planning Director Mollica presented the staff report.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment. As there were no speakers
  present, Mayor Silverstein returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Grisanti moved for requests to be decided by the City Manager
  with guidance from a City Council policy for implementation of AB 2160.

FRIENDLY AMENDMENT
  Councilmember Riggins seconded the motion and moved to direct staff to work
  with the legislature on clarification regarding the statute.

  The maker of the motion accepted the amendment.

  The Council discussed the motion and directed questions to staff.

  The maker and seconder withdrew the motion.

MOTION  Mayor Silverstein moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion to direct
  staff to bring back a resolution which directs that, pursuant to Assembly Bill 2160,
  any fee which must be waived to avoid bypass ofthe City’s permitting processes is
